evidence.finding: Logged-in staffing fell from 49 agents at 09:00 to 44 at 09:15 and reached 33 by 10:30, while scheduled staffing remained 49.
Productive staffing declined from 46 agents at 09:00 to 37 at 09:45 and 31 by 10:45; forecast requirements were 39 agents around the peak.
A center-wide workforce notice at 09:15 explicitly reported multiple same-day absences, matching the onset of the staffing decline.
Service level dropped below the 80% target at 09:15 and remained below target in 10 of the 11 intervals through 11:45, reaching a low of 47.67% at 10:45.
ASA rose from 25.14 seconds at 09:00 to 44.05 seconds at 09:15 and peaked at 80.20 seconds at 10:45.
Abandoned calls increased after the staffing loss, reaching 18 at 10:15 and 23 at 10:45 as reduced capacity failed to keep pace with arrivals.
Across 09:15–11:45, actual offered volume totaled 823 calls versus 841 forecast, so the sustained incident was not caused by an aggregate demand surge.
Total queue staffing matched the center-wide decline, falling from 49 at 09:00 to 44 at 09:15 and 33 by 10:30, with service deterioration subsequently appearing across multiple queues.

primary_root_cause_detail: Multiple same-day absences caused a sustained center-wide loss of logged-in and productive staffing beginning at 09:15. Productive staffing fell from 46 agents at 09:00 to 31 by 10:45, below forecast requirements of 39 agents during the peak period, creating a capacity deficit and sustained service-level degradation.
recommended_actions: Activate same-day absence contingency procedures, including reserve staffing, voluntary overtime, and cross-skilled agent redeployment.
Set real-time alerts when productive staffing falls below interval requirements and escalate before occupancy reaches sustained near-100% levels.
Prioritize queue coverage dynamically during shortages and monitor backlog, ASA, and abandonment until recovery.
Review absence concentration and strengthen intraday staffing buffers for peak intervals.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Actual offered volume over the incident period was below forecast in aggregate; isolated above-forecast intervals do not explain the sustained decline.
Center AHT remained close to the roughly 375-second forecast and did not show a sustained increase aligned with the incident.
Adherence remained broadly stable and generally above 91% after onset, including 96.97% at 10:30; the loss was in available headcount rather than schedule adherence.
Agents in training remained zero throughout the evaluation window.
No routing-change event or transfer-rate increase was supplied, and the staffing loss is directly documented.
Performance varied by queue, but staffing declined across every queue and degradation became broad rather than remaining localized.
No platform event or call-processing disruption was reported, and offered, answered, and abandoned counts remain operationally coherent.
Forecast demand was not materially understated over the incident period; actual aggregate volume was lower than forecast.
Reported service levels reconcile with the supplied formula, and center totals align with queue-level offered and answered counts.

stakeholder_summary: The service-level incident was caused by confirmed same-day absences, not excess demand. Logged-in staffing fell by 16 agents and productive staffing by 15 from pre-incident levels, leaving capacity below forecast requirements during the peak and driving higher waits, abandonment, and sustained service-level failure.
